Guides / 05—08

Check input boundaries, icons and essential graphics

Non-text contrast concerns objects carrying information, rather than every decoration.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Identify essential cues

An input border may be needed to find a field. A check mark, status icon or graph segment may carry meaning. WCAG AA generally calls for 3:1 against adjacent colors for such essential visual information.

Test touching colors

Check an icon against its background and a control outline against surrounding surfaces. Text inside a control is checked separately against text thresholds. Very thin strokes can appear fainter on screen than a solid-color calculation suggests.

Separate decoration

A shadow or ornament not required to understand or operate the interface does not automatically have the same requirement. Record why an element exists so review goes beyond a single page-wide score.

Reproducible example

A white input on a white page needs a visible border when that border is the only cue that the field exists; its label text still needs to be clear.

What to check

A 4.5:1 text ratio does not prove that status icons and input borders are visible.
